cells.tense: You are reading the whole shape of a practice, with your attention in the present.
cells.ask: Say the loose crumb and the piece it belongs with in the same sentence, today, to whoever is doing the work with you.
cells.core:
You can stand back far enough to see the whole shape and still be inside it, working. That's rare — most people get one or the other, the wide view that can't touch the material or the hands that can't say what they're making. You do both over the same bench.

It shows in small things. You name what a piece belongs to mid-build. You hold the far end of the arc in the same breath as the next small task. Nothing about that is forced. This week one piece is asking for something you haven't said yet, and you have the standing to say it plainly: which part belongs with which, out loud, before it looks decided. Say the loose crumb and its whole in one line.
cells.sheetLine: You see how it all hangs together and still work the bench.
cells.verb: sorting what's in front of you into the whole it belongs to
cells.place: where the whole thing hangs together before you say what it is

cells.tense: You are forcing the deadline on a pattern that is still coming together.
cells.ask: Leave the next version of the pattern unnamed for one evening and add one plain improvement to the work you already have.
cells.core:
The reading is racing ahead of the work. You want the whole thing legible by a date you picked, so you keep stepping back to check whether it's finished — and each check widens the frame instead of deepening what you have. The checking gets more of your hours than the work does.

The catch: standing back from this far means you stop touching the material, and the pattern stops being true. It starts to describe the pressure you're under instead of the work. The next step isn't another overview. It's spending one evening doing something specific and slightly better than last time, and leaving the whole shape unnamed until morning. When you come back you'll be looking at an addition, not a verdict.

cells.tense: You stopped standing back to see the pattern, and you are still at that room.
cells.ask: Tell one person the one sentence of what your practice is for, then do one ordinary task as if the whole shape already includes it.
cells.core:
Somewhere you stopped stepping back to look at the whole — not as a decision, it just closed. You found the shape true and found yourself small in front of it, and the stepping back stopped. Now the parts come at you one at a time and none of them belong to anything.

None of that means the looking is gone for good. It means the current through it is thin. The way back doesn't run through the wide view at all — it runs through standing in one thing and saying it out, a single sentence of what it's for, then doing one task in its light. The whole shape gets its current back through the one claim.
cells.sheetLine: The looking stopped, and the parts came apart with it.

cells.tense: You are already reading the whole pattern while telling yourself it's just how the work goes.
cells.ask: Name one call you made last week as a choice you made, then point at the two things it holds together.
cells.core:
You are already reading the whole while you talk as if only the parts are yours. Pick any recent move — a change of order, a cut, the decision to carry on — and it lines up with the rest as if the rest had asked for it. That's a call you're handing to the work itself instead of keeping. You are holding the shape and calling it the shape's own doing.

So the pattern is running, and the one making it isn't in the account. It isn't a confession you're missing. It's one plain sentence said at a table before the day's list, in your own voice: that call was mine. The work you already do gets named by you once, plainly. The pattern is already yours and you already see it.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim in my draft: that the months-long sits or the version-comparisons ever happened — I don't have their history, so I keep every time-reference available rather than asserted, and at Too Little the medicine runs through Assertion, not through Recognition itself. The reader could reasonably say the crash was exhaustion, not a push that ate its own reconstructing. The asks survive a wrong read: saying the crumb out loud, sitting on a call for one evening, naming two twigs as part of one tree, and repeating a single task each day all do real work even if the diagnosis misses. The sentence that serves me more than them is any figure built from the record's vocabulary — artisan, craft, threshold — I'll cut those and pay for the ones I keep with the person's own plain setting.
